title: Justice in the World (1971)
hook: bishops say acting for justice is part of preaching the gospel

segments.voice: Yesterday, Medellín: bishops in Colombia, three kinds of poverty, and a Church that lives alongside the poor. Your line was with the poor. Where did you stand alongside instead of above? Day one thousand three hundred six.

Is working for justice part of the gospel? Or is it something a Christian does afterward, on their own time, once the real religious work is finished? A synod of bishops, gathered in Rome, faced that question head on and gave their answer in a single sentence. Not a footnote, not an appendix at the back, but near the front, where nobody could miss it. The document they produced goes by a plain name. Today's word is Justice in the World.
screen: `PART OF THE GOSPEL, OR AFTER IT?` → `A SYNOD IN ROME.` → `ONE SENTENCE.`

segments.voice: First, the sentence. The bishops wrote that action on behalf of justice, and taking part in transforming the world, appear to them as a constitutive dimension of preaching the gospel. Constitutive is the key word. It means part of what something is, the way flour is part of bread, not sprinkled on top. Preaching the gospel without any concern for justice, on this reading, would be preaching something less than the gospel. Second, an old line behind it. The prophet Micah sums up what God asks, in the Douay-Rheims: "to do judgment, and to love mercy, and to walk solicitous with thy God." Judgment there means justice, doing right by people. It sits in the same breath as mercy and walking with God, not in a separate department. Third, a mirror. The bishops didn't only point outward. They wrote that anyone who dares to speak to others about justice must first be just in their eyes. So they turned to the Church's own house: how it pays the people who work for it, how it uses its property, how it treats people within its own walls. Fourth, the gap. The letter of James pictures a hungry, ill-clothed neighbor, and someone who says to them, in the Douay-Rheims: "Go in peace, be ye warmed and filled", and gives them nothing. Kind words, empty hands. Justice in the World says that gap is not a small one. Words of faith and acts of justice belong in the same sentence.
screen: `A CONSTITUTIVE DIMENSION.` · `DO JUSTICE, LOVE MERCY, WALK WITH GOD.` · `FIRST, BE JUST YOURSELF.` · then, large: `GO IN PEACE, BE YE WARMED AND FILLED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: do one just act. Settle, and breathe. Look over your own day the way the bishops looked over their own house. Is there somebody you owe something to: a fair share of the work, an honest answer, a bill you've been slow to pay, credit you let someone else miss? Is there a small unfairness you could put right before tonight? Don't pick something heroic. Pick something real and doable today. If you pray, you can ask for the courage to do it. If you don't, simply decide. The bell holds the time.
Justice in the World. The synod document saying that acting for justice is a constitutive part of preaching the gospel, beginning with the Church's own house. Today's word.
Your line: justice is gospel. Do the one just act you chose before the day ends, and notice whether anyone else even sees it. Day one thousand three hundred six.

howItsDone: Catholic justice and peace groups, parish social-concerns committees and religious orders often cite Justice in the World as a reason their work for justice belongs at the heart of their faith, not beside it.
